title: Intimacy Pact
concept: An agreement for how you ask for closeness and how you say no, so a no never costs either of you anything, and what each of you actually wants doesn’t stay a guess.
whenToUse: Set it up in advance, on a calm day. Bring it out when asking or saying no has started to feel tense, when things have stalled for weeks, or after a breach that touched this part of the relationship.
steps: Asking? Think first about how it will land for the other person tonight. If you’re declining, you owe nothing. No is enough.
Say out loud: neither of you will punish, sulk, or guilt-trip the other for declining. A no costs nothing and needs no reason.

If it helps, agree how you’ll each say a warm no, and on an alternative you’d both genuinely enjoy — such as holding each other, a kiss goodnight or five minutes of talking. It’s optional and never owed: a no needs no script, reason, or substitute offer, and the pact never creates an obligation.
Each of you names what you actually enjoy and how you like to be approached: body language can signal interest, but ask, and wait for a clear yes.
Revisit the agreement every 30 days. Update it as things change — it’s not a one-time contract, and there’s no keeping score in between.

If a no has been met with pressure or guilt-tripping, stop here and have a Green Rule or Trust Recovery conversation first — don’t try to patch intimacy on top of that. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn’t a ‘once’: go straight to the Help Lines. If it happens again, or either of you feels unable to say no, stop and use the Help Lines. Repeated pressure is never handled with these tools.

phrases.text: I want to be close — not in that space tonight. Can we hold each other?
I’m not there tonight, and it’s not about you. Can we do something together instead?
Not tonight — but I do want to be near you.
Before I think about what I want, I want to know what feels good for you.

working: B says no, plainly. A says “okay” and means it: no cold shoulder, no guilt trip, no sulk at breakfast. The next week, A asks again, lightly.
notWorking: A says no, and B answers with a flat “fine” and the silent treatment. Or B initiates without a thought for whether A is up for it. Either one makes the next honest conversation about it harder.
activity: Write the agreement together — there’s a worksheet for this — and put a real date on the calendar for the 30-day check-in.
warn: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure. If a no is met with pressure once, stop and have a Green Rule or Trust Recovery conversation before anything else. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn’t a ‘once’: go straight to the Help Lines. If a no is met with pressure again, or either of you feels unable to say no, stop and use the Help Lines.
